condition_other: common peroneal nerve injury (CPNI) neuropathic pain model
readout_other: Von Frey filament mechanical nociceptive threshold testing; cytokine protein array (Proteome Profiler Rat Cytokine Array); IL6 and TNFa ELISA
direction_notes: liFUS to the L5 DRG significantly increased mechanical (Von Frey) withdrawal thresholds (reduced allodynia) only in CPNI animals, and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNFa, IL6, IL1b, CNTF, TIMP1) in DRG and dorsal horn while increasing anti-inflammatory IL10.

exposures.label: External liFUS to L5 dorsal root ganglion (DRG)

timing.protocol_description: A single external liFUS treatment (3 min at 8 W) was applied through the skin over the L5 DRG using an external landmark (posterior superior iliac spine), positioned so the beam travelled through soft tissue to the DRG without bony reflection; dose determined from a previously conducted dose-response curve. liFUS reverses allodynic responses in CPNI rats for approximately 3 days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Pre-CPNI (baseline), post-CPNI, and 24 h post-liFUS VFF responses were recorded for the left hind paw (treated) in all four experimental groups. Baseline VFF scores prior to surgery in the CPNI/liFUS cohort were $2 6 . 9 4 \pm 0 . 8 8 \textrm { g } ( \mathrm { n } = 1 6 )$ . Pre-CPNI baseline scores were not significantly different between groups. Significant allodynia was observed following CPNI surgery with VFF scores of $1 . 6 7 \pm 0 . 2 5 ;$ g and $1 . 1 9 \pm 0 . 1 4 \mathrm { \ g }$ in the CPNI/liFUS cohort and CPNI/shamliFUS cohorts, respectively (one-way repeated measure $\mathrm { A N O V A } ; \mathfrak { p } < 0 . 0 0 1 ; \mathfrak { n } = 1 6$ per group). No significant differences from baseline were observed after sham CPNI surgery, with VFF scores of $2 8 . 0 2 ~ \pm ~ 0 . 8 2$ g and $2 6 . 3 9 \pm 1 . 2 0 \mathrm { g }$ in the in the shamCPNI/liFUS and shamCPNI/shamliFUS groups, respectively (one-way repeated measure ANOVA; $\mathrm {  ~ p ~ } > ~ 0 . 0 5 ;$ n = 16 per group). LiFUS treatment alone did not affect baseline responses in the shamCPNI/liFUS cohort, but did significantly reduce allodynia in the CPNI/liFUS cohort $( 2 7 . 0 8 \pm 1 . 2 2 \ : g ;$ One-way repeated measure ANOVA; $\begin{array} { r } { \mathbf { p } < 0 . 0 0 1 ) } \end{array}$ . There was a significant difference of the delta change between pre-liFUS treatment and 24 h after liFUS between the CPNI/liFUS cohort and all other cohorts $\mathbf { \left( p < 0 . 0 0 1 ; \mathrm { F i g . ~ } 1 a \right) }$
source_quotes.sham_type: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (200−300 g; Taconic Farms Germantown, NY) were used for this study. Rats were maintained on a 12 h light dark cycle and provided free access to food and water. Animals were separated into four groups: 1) CPNI/ with liFUS treatment (CPNI/liFUS), 2) CPNI with sham liFUS treatment (CPNI/shamliFUS), 3) sham CPNI with liFUS treatment (shamCPNI/liFUS), and 4) Sham CPNI with sham liFUS treatment (shamCPNI/shamliFUS). All implemented animal protocols were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at Albany Medical College.
source_quotes.anaesthesia: A minimum of 7 days after CPNI or sham CPNI surgeries, the same preparation procedures for anesthesia, with temperature regulation, were used as described above. The left L5 DRG was identified by palpating the L5 lumbar vertebrae. A 3 cm by 3 cm square area of skin, dorsal to the L5 vertebrae was shaved, and Aquasonic 100 ultrasound transmission gel (Parker Laboratories, Fairfield, NJ) was applied to the treatment site. The custom external focused ultrasound device (Acoustic MedSystems Inc, Savoy, IL) was placed using the posterior superior iliac spine as an external landmark (probe is described in more detail in [19]. The animal was then placed in a prone position and the transducer positioned above this external landmark so that the focal point of the probe pointed perpendicular to the spinous process. This allowed the liFUS treatment to travel through soft tissue to reach the DRG target without bony reflection. LiFUS was administered for 3 min at 8 W, with a frequency of 38 Hz, pulse width of 13 ms, and period of 90 ns.This dose was determined by a previously conducted dose response curve [18,46].
source_quotes.direction_notes: Our recent work centers on the use of non-invasive low intensity focused ultrasound (liFUS) to treat neuropathic pain and employs a common peroneal nerve injury (CPNI) rodent model. Delivery of a single external liFUS treatment, directed at the DRG, reverses allodynic responses for 3 days [40]. The mechanism by which liFUS reverses this neuropathic phenotype remains unclear.

flags.reason: Paper states 'a frequency of 38 Hz, pulse width of 13 ms, and period of 90 ns' - these values are internally inconsistent (a 90 ns period implies an ~11 MHz carrier, incompatible with a 13 ms pulse width), and 38 Hz is implausible as an ultrasound carrier frequency. 38 Hz and 13 ms were recorded as PRF and pulse duration respectively per the burst rule reasoning, but the fundamental (carrier) frequency is not clearly stated anywhere in the paper and is left not_reported.

The text labels 38 Hz as 'a frequency' rather than explicitly as PRF; interpreted as PRF because 38 Hz is not a plausible ultrasound carrier frequency, but this is an inference, not a direct statement.
The mechanism of sham liFUS delivery is not described in this paper (only named as 'shamliFUS' groups), so sham_type is set to 'other' per the rule for undescribed sham mechanisms.

VFF behavioral n=16/group is reported for each of the two liFUS-exposed groups (CPNI/liFUS, shamCPNI/liFUS) in each of the two separate cohorts (24h, 72h); no single total across cohorts is stated, so the four group sizes are listed.
No pressure, ISPPA, or ISPTA value is reported anywhere in the paper for the liFUS device; only total acoustic power (8 W) is given.
